title: Mr. Malone
paragraphs: Crime drama based on Craig Rice's lawyer-detective John J. Malone, who solves murders and other mysteries through investigation rather than courtroom procedure.
Crime drama centered on Chicago criminal attorney John J. Malone, created by novelist Craig Rice.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Murder and Mr. Malone / Lovejoy (January 11, 1947 to April 10, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], The Amazing Mr. Malone / Lovejoy (April 24, 1948 to March 26, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], The Amazing Mr. Malone / Gene Raymond (September 21, 1949 to September 24, 1950) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and The Amazing Mr. Malone / George Petrie (May 25, 1951 to July 13, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Bernard L. Schubert (producer and transcriber), Craig Rice (creator), Eugene Wang (writer), George Petrie (performer), Larry Haines (performer), Richard Lewis (director), and Fred Collins (announcer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to Chicago crime and legal world, Craig Rice literary character continuity, criminal defense lawyer investigation, murder investigation, proverb and cliché case-title structure, and network radio crime-drama transition.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar American radio crime and legal drama, 1951 NBC final run, 1948 title change to The Amazing Mr. Malone, and John J. Malone radio actor succession.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|pat-novak-for-hire|Pat Novak, for Hire]], [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|molle-mystery-theatre|Molle Mystery Theatre]].
